H_hierarchical.evidence: The regulatory-signal controller is presented as a flat FSM with S={Go,Yield,Try,Aware}; no parent state or nested sub-FSM is defined.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Table I defines multi-variable guarded transitions, including conjunctions and disjunctions over signal type, omitted id, distance to yielding line, speed, traffic gap, and pedestrian-free timers.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Try asks the trajectory generator to merge before priority traffic or stop; Yield forces stopping before the yielding line; Aware reduces speed; transitions to Go update the omitted signal.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The regulatory FSM has no fault, emergency-stop, rollback, or from-any-state recovery path.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State names, Fig. 4, Table I guards, and the main state-behavior prose are all in Section II.C rather than split across distant sections.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Domain terms such as Must Stop, Right of Way, Pedestrian Crossing, and yielding line are explicitly defined with their required driving behavior.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions for Try, Yield, and Aware are stated in the same regulatory-signal subsection immediately after the transition definitions.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The cyg guard combines two compound cases with OR, each containing several ANDed comparisons over type, distance, speed/gap, and timers.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite state with parent-level entry, during, or exit behavior is described.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: There is no global fault or recovery rule; the shared omit-signal update on return to Go is not a recovery transition.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite state or init pseudo-chain exists in this flat four-state FSM.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There are several guard formulas with boolean composition over typed signals, ids, distances, traffic gaps, vehicle speed, and timers.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The rule that any transition from a non-Go state into Go omits the current regulatory signal applies across Try, Aware, and Yield, creating a shared cross-transition behavior.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: State effects are mostly abstract planner restrictions or trajectory-generator commands rather than concrete actuator I/O, but they are not broad logging/status/notification side effects.

key_nl_quotes: A finite state machine with four possible states
one_line_pitch: A flat but guard-dense autonomous-driving regulatory FSM that stresses guard extraction and state-action attribution more than hierarchy or recovery modeling.
rationale: The sample is a clear state-machine benchmark with strong multi-variable guards and meaningful planner actions. Its main limitation as a top stress test is that it lacks hierarchy and fault recovery, and most information is conveniently co-located in one subsection. It is therefore a useful backup case for guard/action weakness, but not broad enough for the strongest candidate set.
